one_month_reasoning: The Nokia Q3 2026 report on 22 Oct 2026 falls inside the window (Q2 6-K). Management has guided MI gross margin down to 44-46% and FCF conversion toward the low end of 55-75%, so a soft margin print is expected and largely in consensus. In Q2 Nokia beat on OP (434m vs a 376m consensus cited by Inderes [11]) yet fell 5.35% on the day (Twelve Data), so a beat alone does not lift the stock; AI & Cloud orders after Q2's lumpy EUR 2.8bn are the swing factor, and a step-down there is a plausible negative surprise (CEO: 'we should not expect this level of intake every quarter'). Today's +6% came with the AI-optical cohort, not company news, and the stock dropped 13.3% on 14 Sep with no filing, so cohort moves dominate. I take no strong directional view: median $10.75 (about -1%, small giveback after today's jump), log-sd 0.187 (3-month realized vol 63.8% x sqrt(21/252) = 0.184) with a 20% fat-tail component (sd 0.27) for the earnings day.

fair_value.method: 0.65 x P/E leg $8.80 (19.0x Oct-2027 NTM EPS EUR 0.411) + 0.35 x DCF $7.03 (2028 FCF EUR 2.0bn = 3.1bn OP x 65%, 8.58% EUR discount, 2% g) = $8.18 (EUR 7.26), 25% below the $10.84 brief price (a 6 Oct intraday price from the run brief; the official 6 Oct close was $10.975, StockAnalysis NOK history).

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P Global consensus via StockAnalysis, financial currency EUR, last updated 17 Sep 2026 (+19.1% on FY2026 EUR 0.34293). Cross-check: Inderes 2027e adj. EPS EUR 0.39 (Sell-rated house), so consensus is at the top of what independent research supports.

The Infront figures (FY26 OP EUR 2,400m, range 0.32-0.36) were removed by the citation gate: per the run instruction the Infront PDF is treated as unavailable, and no other page shows them.

(CMD 2028 comparable OP top end EUR 3.2bn + net financial income EUR 0.05bn) x (1 - 26.5% tax) / 5,801.9m diluted shares = 3.25 x 0.735 / 5.8019 = EUR 0.412. Top end chosen because FY27 consensus (0.408 x 5.8019 / 0.735 = EUR 3.22bn pre-tax) already sits there. Tax 26.5% = midpoint of FY26 guide ~26-27% (Q2 6-K). Financial income 0.05bn = Inderes 2027e-2028e net financial items (EUR 50m); the FY26 guide of +150-250m is inflated by venture-fund revaluations (Inderes: ~EUR 176m H1 support), so it is not capitalised. No verified FY2028 consensus exists (StockAnalysis FY2028 is paywalled); Inderes 2028e adj. EPS EUR 0.44 is the only published FY28 figure I opened and uses fewer shares (5,597.5m) and 25% tax.

Eleven-peer NTM P/E median 17.88x (range 13.74-43.25x; one basis: StockAnalysis price on 6 Oct 2026 / time-weighted blend of S&P Global current- and next-FY EPS). Segment-mix SOTP: MI = 50.8% of Inderes 2028e segment EBIT (MI 1,725m vs NI 1,673m) at ERIC 13.74x; NI = 49.2% at 27.9x, the NI-sales-weighted (Inderes 2028e Optical 5,226m / IP 3,382m / Fixed 1,980m) mix of CIEN 37.91x for optical, IP median 20.1x (CSCO, HPE, ANET, EXTR) and fixed-access median 14.6x (CALX, ADTN, HLIT) -> 20.7x. 19x is the average of median and SOTP (19.3x) rounded down: the SOTP gives Nokia optical a Ciena multiple although Nokia's NI margin target (13-17%) and Inderes NI growth (8-11%/yr) are well below Ciena's (+65% next-FY EPS), and comparable EPS excludes restructuring that keeps recurring (Inderes NRIs 2027e -620m, 2028e -450m; Q2 2026 reported EPS 0.00 vs comparable 0.07). 19x is inside the peer range, a 6% premium to the median justified only by the profit mix, which is structural (CMD Optical+IP 10-12% CAGR target).
ECB reference rate 6 Oct 2026; NOK ADR = 1 ordinary share.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: 2028 FCF EUR 2.015bn (OP 3.1bn x 65%) growing 4%/yr to 2032, discount 8.58% (EUR AAA 10Y 3.50% + 1.2 x ERP 4.23%), terminal g 2.0%, valued at Oct-2027; EV EUR 33.44bn + net cash 2.776bn = EUR 36.22bn / 5.8019bn = EUR 6.24 = $7.03

inputs_detail.derivation: Upper half of CMD 2028 target EUR 2.7-3.2bn; FY27 consensus already implies ~EUR 3.2bn pre-tax and Inderes 2028e adj. EBIT is 3,257m, so 3.1bn is a skeptic haircut of ~0.1bn to the top end.

Low end of CMD 65-75% target: Nokia is tracking the low end of its 2026 55-75% range (CFO, Q2 call) and restructuring cash keeps flowing (Inderes NRIs 2028e -450m). 3.1 x 0.65 = EUR 2.015bn; cross-check Inderes 2028e FCFF EUR 2,064m (difference 2%).
Inderes FCFF 2028e-2032e 2,064 / 2,237 / 2,286 / 2,348 / 2,500m = ~4.9% CAGR; CMD NI growth 6-8% offset by ~1% MI growth (Inderes). Rounded down to 4%.

EUR cash flows discounted at a EUR rate: euro-area AAA 10Y spot 3.50% (ECB, 5 Oct 2026) + beta 1.2 x implied ERP 4.23% (Damodaran, 2025) = 8.58%. Beta 1.2 = Inderes equity beta, above StockAnalysis 5Y beta 0.77, for the AI-order cyclicality. Net-cash company, so cost of equity = WACC. Cross-check Inderes WACC 8.2%.
EUR nominal long-run growth; equals Inderes terminal growth; below the 3.50% EUR risk-free rate.

Net cash and interest-bearing financial investments at 30 Jun 2026, held flat to Oct 2027 (Inderes forecasts 3.34bn net cash at end-2027, i.e. upside; not used because it depends on unconfirmed FCF timing).

PV of 2028-2032 FCF (2.015, 2.096, 2.179, 2.267, 2.357bn; mid-year, t = 0.75..4.75 yrs from Oct-2027) = EUR 8.71bn; TV = 2.357 x 1.02 / (0.0858 - 0.02) = EUR 36.56bn, PV EUR 24.73bn; + net cash 2.776 = EUR 36.22bn / 5.8019bn = EUR 6.24 x 1.1269 = $7.03. Cross-check Inderes DCF EUR 6.5. Sensitivity: 70% conversion -> $7.53; 7.73% discount (beta 1.0) -> $7.99.
ECB reference rate 6 Oct 2026; NOK ADR = 1 ordinary share.

bear.story: AI & Cloud intake proves lumpy or partly pulled forward (CEO: 'we should not expect this level of intake every quarter'; only ~half of Q2's EUR 2.8bn converts within 12 months), Mobile Infrastructure margin slips (Q3 GM guided 44-46%) and radio/core weakness shows once licensing is stripped out (Light Reading). 2028 OP lands at the CMD low end EUR 2.7bn -> EPS (2.7 + 0.05) x 0.735 / 5.8019 = EUR 0.348; the market pays the low-growth telecom-equipment cluster (avg of ERIC 13.7x, HLIT 14.3x, ADTN 14.6x, HPE 15.2x = 14.5x) = EUR 5.05 = $5.69.

base.story: Consensus is delivered (FY27 EPS EUR 0.41, 2028 at the CMD top end; NTM EPS EUR 0.411 at Oct-2027). The multiple compresses only part of the way from today's 24.5x NTM toward the 20.7x segment-mix multiple, because valuation gaps close slowly and Nokia trades with the AI-optical cohort: 22.0x x 0.411 = EUR 9.04 = $10.19, about -6% vs today.

bull.story: AI & Cloud orders keep converting and optical capacity expansions land, pushing 2028 OP to ~EUR 3.6bn, 12% above the CMD top end -> EPS EUR 0.462 (cross-check Inderes 2029e EPS 0.47); the market prices all of Nokia at its NI peer-mix multiple 27.9x (CIEN/IP/fixed weighted) = EUR 12.90 = $14.54, short of the June 2026 high of $17.45.

Excluded: LITE, COHR, FN, GLW (components/materials); ZTE (vendor data internally inconsistent and price stale for Golden Week); RBBN (EPS collapse to $0.06 makes P/E meaningless); MSI and UI (software/services-heavy or asset-light models with structurally higher margins and lower cyclicality).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 19.0x NTM on Oct-2027 EPS: inside the range, +6% vs the 17.88x median, below the 20.7x segment-mix SOTP; NOK today is at 24.5x, a 37% premium to the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The only persistent reason for any premium is profit mix: about half of 2028e segment EBIT is Network Infrastructure (Inderes), where the relevant peers trade at 14.6x (fixed) to 37.9x (optical), and the CMD targets Optical+IP growth of 10-12% a year to 2028, which is structural. Against it, three persistent negatives: (1) comparable EPS excludes restructuring that keeps recurring (EUR 800m charges in 2026 per the Q2 6-K; Inderes NRIs -620m in 2027e and -450m in 2028e); (2) cash conversion is at the low end (CFO); (3) NI margin targets of 13-17% are well below optical/AI peers. Net, I take the midpoint of median and SOTP (19.3x) rounded down to 19x. Sell-side ratings (StockAnalysis PT $14.97 from 14 analysts; Inderes Sell EUR 6.50; Santander Underperform EUR 6.85) are not used to set the multiple.

thesis_break_reason: $6.33 = EUR 5.61 = Ericsson's verified NTM multiple (13.74x) on FY2027 consensus EPS EUR 0.408, i.e. zero value for the AI & Cloud optical/IP premium on unchanged earnings. It is 35% below the 23 Jul post-Q2 close ($9.73) and 34% below the 14 Sep panic low ($9.65). Trading there most likely means the earnings base itself is breaking (AI & Cloud orders reversing or cancelled, FY26 guide cut below EUR 2.1bn, or the EUR 2.7-3.2bn 2028 target abandoned), not 62%-vol noise; the bear scenario ($5.69) then becomes the base.

reasoning: Facts: NOK $10.84 = EUR 9.62 at ECB 1.1269; 5,801.9m diluted shares -> market cap ~EUR 55.8bn; net cash EUR 2.78bn (Q2 6-K). Today's NTM EPS is EUR 0.393 (0.236 x FY26 0.343 + 0.764 x FY27 0.408), so NOK trades at 24.5x NTM against an 11-peer NTM median of 17.88x on one basis. Round-2 changes: (1) I rebuilt the peer set as the supervisor asked, using one NTM basis because the peers' fiscal years end in Jun/Jul/Oct/Dec; ERIC's SEK EPS is converted at the ECB cross (9.98). (2) The S&P FCF figure is gone. The DCF now uses CMD conversion at its 65% low end x EUR 3.1bn OP = EUR 2.0bn, which matches Inderes FCFF 2028e of EUR 2,064m, discounted at a EUR rate (3.50% + 1.2 x 4.23% = 8.58%) -> $7.03; Inderes's own DCF is EUR 6.5. (3) FY28 EPS is capped at the CMD top end (0.412); I disagree with the supervisor's +0.15bn financial income because the 2026 figure includes venture-fund revaluations (Inderes ~176m in H1). P/E leg 19x x 0.411 = $8.80. FV = 0.65 x 8.80 + 0.35 x 7.03 = $8.18. Skeptic findings: no short report and short interest of only 1.25% of float; credit is not the issue (net cash; S&P positive outlook per secondary press); the CEO's April purchase was plan-linked. The real bear case is earnings quality and valuation: comparable vs reported EPS (Q2 0.07 vs 0.00), recurring restructuring, low-end cash conversion, Light Reading's doubt about radio/core profitability, Inderes Sell (TP EUR 6.50; P/E 25x/23x 2026e/27e) and Santander Underperform. The consensus PT of $14.97 (14 analysts) is the bull counterweight; I treat it as evidence of sentiment, not value. Reconciliation: FV $8.18 is cash-flow value. The scenarios are market-price outcomes: bear $5.69 (0.30), base $10.19 (0.50; 22x, so only half of the premium to the 20.7x mix multiple closes in 12 months, since the stock trades with the AI-optical cohort), bull $14.54 (0.20). Their probability-weighted mean is $9.71, $1.53 above FV; that gap is the value of the market continuing to price comparable EPS while ignoring restructuring cash. The ladder is a mixture of three lognormals (log-sd 0.34 each, mean equal to each scenario price; total log-sd 0.48, below the 62-64% realized vol because the scenarios carry the fundamental dispersion). It gives a median of $8.85, a mean of ~$9.71, P(close >= FV) = 0.56 and P(>= $10.84) = 0.338. Research limits: sec.gov refused scripted access (read through WebFetch); peer forward EBITDA and NOK FY2028 consensus are paywalled; the S&P report was not reachable.

revisions.to: 11 systems/telecom-networking peers on NTM P/E; median 17.88x
revisions.why: Supervisor comps_review (7 systems peers, FY2027 median 15.1x). I add HLIT, EXTR, VIAV and IDCC so there are 11 genuine comparables (IDCC covers Technology Standards), and use NTM to align fiscal years (CSCO Jul, EXTR/VIAV Jun, CIEN/HPE Oct). On my basis the supervisor's seven give 16.0x; the added four lift the median to 17.9x.

Multiples re-anchored to the consistent peer basis (bear at the 14.5x telecom-equipment cluster instead of 17x; bull at the 27.9x NI peer mix instead of 28x on a 24x median); bear EPS from the CMD low end; probabilities unchanged at 0.30/0.50/0.20.

Lower scenario centres from the corrected peer basis; component log-sd raised from 0.30-0.33 to 0.34 (mixture total 0.48) because my own Twelve Data computation shows realized vol of 61.7% (1y), 71.0% (6m) and 63.8% (3m), so the post-spike period is not calmer.
Re-based on the verified ERIC NTM multiple: 13.74x x FY2027 consensus EUR 0.408 x 1.1269 = $6.33; supervisor's $6.50 rests on ERIC 13.6x FY27, close to this.
3-month realized vol 63.8% x sqrt(21/252) = 0.184 (own computation; supervisor 65%), with a fat-tail component for the 22 Oct Q3 report.
